subject: Economics
description: India's planning era: Planning Commission, key plans, Niti Aayog, themes

questions.stem: FIRST FIVE YEAR PLAN of India (1951-56) gave priority to:

options.option_text: Agriculture + irrigation (Harrod-Domar model)
Heavy industries (Mahalanobis model later)
IT + services sector (came much later)
Defence + nuclear programme alone

questions.explanation: FIRST PLAN (1951-56) — focused on AGRICULTURE + IRRIGATION + power (recovery from Partition + Bengal famine 1943). Based on HARROD-DOMAR growth model (savings → investment → output → growth). Targets: ~2.1% GDP growth (achieved 3.6%, exceeded target). KEY PROJECTS: Bhakra-Nangal (Punjab), Hirakud (Odisha), Damodar Valley Corp (DVC, WB-Jharkhand). 2nd PLAN (1956-61) — MAHALANOBIS MODEL — heavy industry focus (steel, machine tools, electricity). 'BEYOND THIS HARROD-DOMAR' — built capital goods sector first, hence consumer goods later. STEEL plants set up: BHILAI (USSR), DURGAPUR (UK), ROURKELA (Germany). Modi-era ABOLISHED Planning Commission (replaced by NITI Aayog 2015). 12 plans total ran 1951-2017.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: PLANNING COMMISSION was set up in 1950 by:

options.option_text: Cabinet Resolution (Nehru chaired it)
Constitutional provision in Schedule
Act of Parliament (statutory body)
Presidential Order under emergency

questions.explanation: PLANNING COMMISSION — set up 15 March 1950 by CABINET RESOLUTION (NOT Constitution; not a statutory body). PM as ex-officio CHAIRMAN. Drew inspiration from Soviet planning. Formulated Five-Year Plans, advised on resource allocation. CRITICISM (over time): top-down 'one size fits all'; ignored states' diversity; bureaucratic; relevance declined post-1991 liberalisation. ABOLISHED 1 Jan 2015 by Modi govt. REPLACED by NITI AAYOG (National Institution for Transforming India) — also non-statutory; 'cooperative federalism' approach (not directive); think tank role. PM = Chairperson; CMs of states + LGs of UTs in GOVERNING COUNCIL; CEO + Vice Chairperson run day-to-day. NITI Aayog: SDG India Index, Aspirational Districts Programme, Atal Innovation Mission.

questions.stem: GREEN REVOLUTION in India (1960s-70s) is primarily associated with:

options.option_text: M.S. Swaminathan (father of GR in India)
Verghese Kurien (White Revolution dairy)
Hargobind Khorana (genetics, Nobel)
C.N.R. Rao (chemistry, Bharat Ratna)

questions.explanation: GREEN REVOLUTION (1960s-70s) — dramatic increase in food grain output. Pioneered globally by NORMAN BORLAUG (American agronomist, Nobel Peace 1970, dwarf wheat varieties); brought to INDIA by M.S. SWAMINATHAN (father of Green Revolution in India; Bharat Ratna 2024 posthumous). KEY ELEMENTS: HYV seeds (high-yield variety, Mexican wheat + IRRI rice), CHEMICAL FERTILIZERS, IRRIGATION, mechanisation (tractors, threshers). FOCUS STATES: Punjab, Haryana, Western UP — mostly wheat; later rice in Andhra, TN. RESULT: India self-sufficient in grain by mid-1970s; PL 480 wheat imports from USA stopped. WHITE REVOLUTION = MILK production (Verghese Kurien, AMUL, Operation Flood, ~1970+). BLUE = fish; YELLOW = oilseed; PINK = onion; SILVER = poultry/eggs.

questions.stem: MAHALANOBIS MODEL (basis for 2nd Five Year Plan) emphasised:

options.option_text: Heavy industry + capital goods first
Agriculture + small-scale only
Services sector exports primarily
Foreign direct investment as priority

questions.explanation: P.C. MAHALANOBIS — Indian statistician, founder of INDIAN STATISTICAL INSTITUTE (ISI, 1931). Designed 2ND PLAN (1956-61). Logic: build CAPITAL GOODS (machines that make machines) first → enables faster long-term growth than starting with consumer goods. Inspired by Soviet planning (Feldman model). PHASE 1: heavy + machine-building industry. PHASE 2: consumer goods. CRITICISM: ignored demand-side, agricultural neglect, foreign exchange shortage. INDIA's stable BUT slow 'HINDU RATE OF GROWTH' (~3.5% annual, 1950-80) often blamed on this. PROFESSIONALLY he's known for MAHALANOBIS DISTANCE (statistics). 'PLANNED ECONOMY' phase ended ~1991 with LPG reforms. POLICY trade-off question: should developing economies focus on heavy industry first or agri/services? — debated still.

questions.stem: PLAN HOLIDAY (1966-69) — period when normal Five-Year Plans were SUSPENDED — was due to:

options.option_text: 1965 Indo-Pak war + drought + economic crisis
Indira Gandhi's 1975 Emergency declared
1991 BoP crisis when reserves crashed
Demonetisation of currency in 2016

questions.explanation: PLAN HOLIDAY (1966-1969) — three ANNUAL PLANS replaced 4th FYP. CAUSES: (1) 1965 INDO-PAK WAR (drained resources); (2) successive DROUGHTS (1965, 1966) → near-famine; (3) DEVALUATION OF RUPEE (June 1966, INR/$ from 4.76 to 7.50 — 36% devaluation, controversial); (4) PL 480 wheat imports from USA → political dependency under LBJ's 'short-tether' policy. 4th PLAN (1969-74) under Indira → focus on POVERTY ALLEVIATION + self-reliance. 'GARIBI HATAO' (1971 Indira election slogan). Other notable plan disruptions: ROLLING PLAN (1978-80) under Janata govt (1979-80 Annual Plan). PLAN ALMOST TERMINATED 1990 (BoP crisis); 9th Plan (1997-2002) only after delay.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: 12th and FINAL Five Year Plan of India (2012-17) had a theme of:

options.option_text: Faster, sustainable, more inclusive growth
Self-reliance + heavy industry only
Agriculture-led growth with no industry
Defence-only spending without anything else

questions.explanation: 12TH PLAN (2012-2017) — last FYP; THEME: 'Faster, more inclusive, and sustainable growth'. Targets: 8% GDP growth (achieved ~7%), reduce poverty 10 pp, create 50 million jobs, focus on ENERGY-WATER-AGRI sustainability. Approved on Dec 2012. ABOLISHED Planning Commission Jan 2015 by Modi → no 13th Plan. NITI AAYOG since 2015 — 'cooperative + competitive federalism'; works on STRATEGIES (3-year action agenda, 7-year strategy, 15-year vision). Key initiatives: SDG India Index, Atal Innovation Mission, AIIMS expansion, district-level competitiveness rankings ('Aspirational Districts'). FINANCING: 14th Finance Commission (2015-20, headed by Y.V. Reddy) — increased states' share of central taxes from 32% to 42% — major fiscal devolution.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: NITI AAYOG (since 2015) replaces Planning Commission. NITI stands for:

options.option_text: National Institution for Transforming India
National Institute for Trade in India
National Investment Tribunal of India
National Inclusion Trust for Industries

questions.explanation: NITI AAYOG = NATIONAL INSTITUTION FOR TRANSFORMING INDIA. Set up 1 JAN 2015 (Cabinet resolution; not statutory). REPLACES Planning Commission. STRUCTURE: PM = Chairperson; VICE CHAIRPERSON (full-time, currently Suman Bery — appointed 2022); GOVERNING COUNCIL (PM + all CMs of states + LGs of UTs + ex-officio members); FULL-TIME MEMBERS + part-time members + special invitees. CEO (currently BVR Subrahmanyam, appointed 2023). KEY PROGRAMMES: NITI FORUM for North East, ASPIRATIONAL DISTRICTS (112 backwards districts, with rankings), ATAL INNOVATION MISSION (Atal Tinkering Labs, Incubators), SDG India Index, India Innovation Index, Composite Water Index. CONTRAST with Planning Commission: ADVISORY (no fund allocation power); cooperative federalism (consult states); shorter horizon (3-7-15 year plans).

questions.stem: Which Five Year Plan was prematurely terminated by the Janata government in 1977–78 and replaced with 'Rolling Plans'?

options.option_text: Third Five Year Plan (1961-66), India's largest agricultural plan
Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79), originally drafted by D.P. Dhar
Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74), focused on agricultural self-reliance
Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-85), launched after the Emergency period ended

questions.explanation: The 5th Five Year Plan (1974-79) was scrapped one year before its scheduled close (March 1978) by the Janata government, which introduced Rolling Plans for 1978-83. When Congress returned under Indira Gandhi in 1980, Rolling Plans were discarded and the 6th Plan (1980-85) was launched. Option C (4th Plan) is wrong because it ended in 1974, three years before the Janata government came to power.

questions.stem: The nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks in India took place on 19 July 1969. This historic event occurred during which Five Year Plan period?

options.option_text: Third Five Year Plan (1961-66), which closed in 1966 before nationalisation
Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79), during India's peak socialist policy phase
Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74), starting in the very year of nationalisation
Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-85), coinciding with the return of Congress to power

questions.explanation: The 4th Five Year Plan commenced on 1 April 1969; bank nationalisation happened on 19 July 1969 — firmly within this plan. Option A (3rd Plan) is factually ruled out because it ended in 1966, three years before nationalisation. Option B (5th Plan) is the classic trap: the 5th Plan is associated with socialist policy, but 1969 falls in the 4th Plan, not the 5th (which started only in 1974).

questions.stem: India's Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97) is described as the first plan to adopt 'indicative planning.' Which of the following BEST describes what 'indicative planning' means in this context?

options.option_text: Planning targets shifted focus from heavy industry to IT and services sectors
The Plan set non-binding growth targets, leaving execution largely to market forces
Central government formally gave up its power to direct state-level allocations
Sectoral targets were retained but enforcement responsibility shifted to Panchayati Raj bodies

questions.explanation: Post-1991 LPG reforms fundamentally changed planning: instead of mandatory production directives to industries, the government set broad growth goals and let market forces guide resource allocation — that is 'indicative planning.' Option C is a distractor: state allocation continued via the Gadgil Formula and is a separate mechanism; it was not surrendered. Option D conflates indicative planning with decentralisation under the 73rd Amendment.

questions.stem: The 'Minimum Needs Programme (MNP),' which guaranteed basic services such as primary education, rural drinking water, rural roads and housing for agricultural workers, was FIRST introduced in India under which Five Year Plan?

options.option_text: Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74), following the nationalisation of banks
Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79), alongside the removal-of-poverty agenda
Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-85), under the 20-Point Programme framework
Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90), focusing on food, work and productivity

questions.explanation: MNP was introduced in the 5th Five Year Plan (1974-79) to provide a guaranteed floor level of basic services to all citizens. It covered rural drinking water, primary health, primary education, housing for landless labour, rural roads, electrification and nutrition. Option C is the most common error: the 6th Plan revived and extended poverty programmes (including IRDP and NREP) and relaunched the 20-Point Programme, but MNP itself was conceived and launched in the 5th Plan.

questions.stem: The 'Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP),' once India's largest self-employment scheme targeting rural BPL households through subsidised credit and productive asset transfer, was universally launched at the outset of which Five Year Plan?

options.option_text: Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79), as part of Indira Gandhi's anti-poverty programmes
Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90), alongside JRY and food-for-work programmes
Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-85), marking a shift to direct anti-poverty asset transfers
Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74), launched in the wake of the 1971 elections mandate

questions.explanation: IRDP was universally launched on 2 October 1980 (Gandhi Jayanti), at the very start of the 6th Five Year Plan (1980-85). It provided government subsidies and bank loans to rural BPL families to acquire productive assets for self-employment. Option A (5th Plan) is the classic trap because the 5th Plan had the MNP and the original 20-Point Programme — but IRDP as a distinct, nationwide scheme came only in October 1980 under the 6th Plan.

questions.stem: Under the original Gadgil Formula (applied from the Fourth Five Year Plan for allocating Central Plan Assistance to general-category states), which single criterion carried the HIGHEST percentage weightage?

options.option_text: Per capita income gap from richest state — assigned 25% weightage in the formula
Population based on 1971 Census enumeration — assigned 60% weightage in the formula
State own-tax effort relative to taxable capacity — assigned 20% weightage
Special backward area and tribal belt problems — assigned 30% weightage

questions.explanation: The original Gadgil Formula (1969) distributed weightage as: Population 60%, Per Capita Income (inverse) 10%, Tax Effort 10%, Ongoing Projects 10%, Special Problems 10%. Population dominated at 60% to ensure resource flows matched the sheer scale of demographic need. Option A is the most tempting trap: in the later Modified Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula, the income-distance criterion gained substantially more weight (25%), but in the original 1969 formula it was only 10%.

questions.stem: The 'Bharat Nirman' programme — covering rural housing, safe drinking water, rural electrification, rural roads, rural telephony, and irrigation as its six verticals — was announced in the Union Budget and formally launched during which Five Year Plan?

options.option_text: Ninth Five Year Plan (1997-2002), under PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee's NDA government
Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12), as a flagship initiative under inclusive growth
Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97), coinciding with post-liberalisation rural reforms
Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07), announced in Union Budget 2005-06 by P. Chidambaram

questions.explanation: Bharat Nirman was announced by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in the Union Budget of 2005-06 as a four-year business plan (2005-09), placing it squarely within the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07). Option B (11th Plan) is the most common error: because many Bharat Nirman targets extended into the 11th Plan period and it received continued funding, candidates mistakenly associate its launch with 2007-12 — but the announcement, targets and initial expenditure clearly belong to the 10th Plan.
